page: Microsoft Azure E160as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. The instance provisions 160 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 80 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by 1280.0 GB of RAM. This provides a consistent 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, along with support for vector extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. There are no dedicated GPUs included, and local storage is marked as None, meaning persistent storage must be attached via network-based Azure storage.

Across benchmark measurements, the instance routinely scores in the top 10% tier. Multi-core compute performance is demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 29149.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 286658.75, supplemented by a PassMark CPU score of 145445.76. In memory-intensive benchmarks, uncached large-block read operations reached 462.89 GB/sec while write operations achieved 209.83 GB/sec. Data manipulation metrics also place the server in the highest performance percentiles, registering 196.39 million Redis SET operations per second, a PassMark database score of 40507.49, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 1033.56 GB/sec. On CPU-based inference, the system generated 72.2 tokens per second on a 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of 160 compute threads alongside 1.28 TB of memory minimizes per-gigabyte overhead for large-scale monolithic deployments. However, the absence of bundled local storage introduces an operational tradeoff, as disk I/O performance relies on external storage configuration. The instance is suited for enterprise in-memory databases, real-time analytics platforms, large-scale Redis deployments, and memory-heavy scientific simulations.

The instance does not include bundled GPUs or local disk storage, necessitating remote storage solutions.
